topic: SimdVF RMSNorm works end to end; w preconversion helps; still below parity

results.single_row: D=4096 single row: SimdVF kernel matches CPU float64 exactly (max_abs 0.0)
results.multi_core: batch 512, 64 cores, rows=4, two-pass: correct, rel err 0.00119 <= 2^-7
results.timing_first: kernel 0.12667 ms vs vendor 0.06825 ms -> ratio 0.539 (5 interleaved samples each)
results.timing_wpreconvert: preconverting w to f32 once gave kernel 0.1234 ms -> ratio 0.581 (5 interleaved samples each)

comparison.delta: SimdVF is materially faster than SimtVF on this shape

status: a correct SimdVF kernel exists and is faster than the SimtVF one, but is still ~0.58x of the vendor; the target is >=1.0 with bootstrap lower bound >=0.98
unknowns: pipe attribution (vec vs mte2 vs mte3) not yet measured for this kernel
vendor reading varies by window (0.068-0.072 ms here vs ~0.05 earlier)
not_proven: no per-shape parity; no acceptance; readings are a single process and not witness-audited
review_correction: The historical interpretation claiming a proven bottleneck, performance ceiling, compiler-wide limitation, or cross-run speedup is retracted. The measurements were exploratory and insufficiently paired; profiler utilization is not a proof of a hard bound. The archived candidate initially used an invalid dtype spelling and must be verified separately. Preserve numerical observations as historical only.
